title: spec: an `oauth2` `authorization_code` instance takes its OAuth client from the installer (a per-connection client record), not a packaged `clientId` — ADR-0143 D2.1 amendment (#28702 B)
body:
epic:#27293#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVBKAFk1ntXSjvPt7U

Filing gate: ④ execution of a maintainer ruling, slice 1 of 3 (the spec slice; it goes first). Ruling-ref: 6566728470 (#28702, letter B, maintainer 「同意」 2026-11-02T01:12Z). Child of #27293 (E4). Handed to the spec lane per the maintainer's 「按你的方案交给车道」 (2026-11-01). ⛔ Not a claim.

Ruling-ref: 6566728470

## What the ruling binds

An open-edition OAuth connector app ships no ObjectStack-owned `clientId` or secret. The administrator of each deployment registers their own integration key with the vendor, against that deployment's callback (`OS_BASE_URL` / `OS_AUTH_URL` + `/api/v1/automation/connectors/oauth/callback`), and enters it on the connection. Shape: a per-connection client record on the `authorization_code` instance, the shape ADR-0143 D2.1 already keeps for MCP dynamic registration (`registered_client`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-connector-connection.object.ts:87`). It is a widening: `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`.

## Work (this slice)

- `packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts` (the `authorization_code` variant, ~`:319-345` at `origin/main` `67103cc1`). Today `clientId` is a packaged literal (`:301-303`). Add the declared way for the instance to say its client comes from the installer, and how a packaged `clientId` relates to it: refused, or kept for private apps. That choice is this slice's to make and must say why. Keep the definition free of secrets.
- `docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md` § D2: amend D2.1 to say what the variant carries and where an installer-supplied client lives. This is Tier H and needs a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval.
- Generated surfaces and any ledger rows the spec gates require. The review runs at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
- Confidence gap carried from the ruling: DocuSign's per-account production API host comes from vendor docs and was not measured. Say how a host is discovered, or name production as a follow-up.

## Reader

The spec lane takes it from `pm:queue`. The server slice and the ui slice are `Blocked-by:` this card. DocuSign (#28277) waits on all three.

The 500 most recent issues and PRs (read 2026-11-02T02:03Z), titles grepped for `client ?id|oauth client|installer-supplied|integration key`: 1 hit, #28702 (the decision itself). Control `oauth`: 9 hits.
